messages:
Samir Khan: Quick proposal — add a lightweight severity layer (info / warn / error / critical) that we attach as telemetry tags (severity:<level>) and surface as console badges + SDK error.severity. Would help dashboard filtering and automated escalations. Thoughts?

Lucy Park: 👍 yes. We need an explicit mapping table from status codes -> severity. Also decide what to do about service-level vs tenant-level escalation.

Anna Morales: We should avoid lumping all 4xx into the same bucket. 401/403 are auth/policy -> usually 'info' or 'warn'. 4xx due to client payload (e.g., schema error) could be 'warn' but not 'error'.

Devin O'Neill: Agreed. Quick rules: 2xx = info, 3xx = info, 4xx = warn (split by 401/403 -> info/warn), 429 = warn (with retry_hint), 5xx = error/critical depending on downstream vs transient.

Kevin Zhao: Console UX: badges as color tokens: info=green, warn=amber, error=red, critical=purple. Add a severity filter in the top nav and a severity column in request logs.

Samir Khan: Sketch mapping (proposal):
```json
{
  "2xx": "info",
  "3xx": "info",
  "400": "warn",
  "401": "info",
  "403": "info",
  "404": "warn",
  "409": "warn",
  "429": "warn",
  "5xx_transient": "error",
  "5xx_systemic": "critical"
}
```
This is intentionally high-level; we'll refine rules for systemic vs transient 5xx.

Anna Morales: SDK change suggestion: expose error.severity and error.code_category (client|auth|quota|infra). Keep backward compatibility — defaults to previous behavior when not present.

Devin O'Neill: I'll own the SDK PR. Plan: add error.severity to response envelope in minor version; no breaking changes to payload shape. Server will tag events even for older SDKs so telemetry is complete.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: created canary rollout job (/error-severity-rollout) -> 5% hosts.

Lucy Park: Rollout plan: 1) server-side telemetry tags only (no UI) -> 2) add console filters + badges -> 3) SDK exposure -> 4) docs + changelog. Canary: 5% -> 25% -> 100%.

Kevin Zhao: Operational question: do we want automatic escalation rules (e.g., convert repeated warn -> critical after X occurrences) or keep escalation manual? Auto rules are handy but can generate noise.

Samir Khan: I'm leaning thresholded escalation: e.g., tenant-level 5 occurrences in 1 minute => escalate to critical for alerting. We'll tune thresholds per route. Add as part of alerting policy.

Anna Morales: I'll draft a short runbook snippet for ops. Example query to locate criticals: `event.type:request AND severity:critical` — will add dashboard sample.

Devin O'Neill: Action items: I'll open SDK PR (owner), Anna writes runbook + example queries, Kevin implements console badges + filter, Samir to finalize mapping and approve.

Samir Khan: Quick vote — +1 if you agree with the proposed mapping/plan :thumbsup:

Lucy Park: :thumbsup:

Kevin Zhao: :thumbsup:

Anna Morales: :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary successful on 2024-11-04T18:12:00Z, promoting to 25% now.

Samir Khan: Thanks all — will post the finalized mapping doc and RFC draft in #eng-platform later today.
